title: Bank of America Spends Hundreds of Millions on AI Security Patching in Q3
summary:
Bank of America recorded additional Q3 expenses totaling several hundred million dollars to address anti-money laundering compliance and security vulnerabilities uncovered by the Mythos AI model from Anthropic. To resolve the flaws in both proprietary and vendor software, the bank hired 1,000 external contractors to support 3,000 internal employees. CEO Brian Moynihan told CNBC that the bank brought in this "army" of external help to patch the code after the AI models exposed the gaps.

Anthropic has since expanded its 'Cyber Mission' for open-source software, reporting that its OSS Scanner had approximately 650 applicants and 114 accepted projects in 11 days. The scanner found 77 critical and 803 high-severity findings during that period, though the company has struggled with human review bottlenecks, triaging only 6,000 of 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities found over six months. The startup also continues its Critical Infrastructure Defense Program with partners such as Hitachi, CrowdStrike, and Palo Alto Networks.
